headline: OpenAI watermarks ChatGPT outputs by default in the EU
summary: The company is complying with the EU AI Act, but the watermarking method is proprietary and can be circumvented.
details: OpenAI is implementing automatic watermarking for ChatGPT-generated text within the European Union, a move driven by the EU AI Act's requirement to mark AI-produced content.

This new feature, called textGrain, embeds imperceptible patterns in word choices that can be detected by a specialized tool. While OpenAI aims for a 92% detection rate in ideal conditions, tests show that altering just 10% of the text can reduce detection success by nearly 30%, and 20% alteration can drop it by 75%.

The watermarking is designed to comply with regulations, but like other solutions, it is not foolproof and can be circumvented with basic technical know-how. The detection rate is also lower for shorter or translated texts.

Outside the EU, the watermarking feature will be available but will not be enabled by default. OpenAI plans to grant access to its detector to select researchers and organizations, with a process for others to apply over time.

This contrasts with competitor Anthropic, which has enabled watermarking globally for its models. OpenAI's watermarking is currently focused on ChatGPT and Codex apps, with optional availability in the API.
